*long review, but hopefully it'll help someone like me!* I'm 31, but when I was 22 I was diagnosed with cystic hormonal acne. absolutely nothing topical worked for me, and I was put on an oral medication that has kept me *mostly* clear for nearly a decade. specific times of the month, I usually would break out here and there, but nothing severe. I've been washing my face 2x a day with just a basic 2% SA cleanser for as long as I can remember. about 2 months ago, something happened with my skin. A combination of a new foundation and hormones wreaked absolute havoc on my skin, and I could not get it under control. my pimples weren't cystic- the acne I have now is very different from the acne I had at 22. I have a lot of texture, redness, and small bright red zits rather than the deep, large and painful cysts I had at 22. my skin became incredibly sensitive to products id been using for a while, and I had to start completely over with finding skincare that wouldn't break me out. I spent so much money on different moisturizers and serums, but they were all SA acne products and they did absolutely nothing for me (I'm assuming because I've been using a SA cleanser for so many years) and my skin was just getting worse. I picked this up because it has benzoyl peroxide in it, which is an active ingredient I hadn't tried yet. I purchased this product on 11/7, so a little over two weeks ago, and I'm FINALLY seeing clarity in my skin! all of my closed comedones and texture are nearly gon

[I received this product in exchange for my honest review] I recently started using the La Roche-Posay Effaclar Duo Dual Action Acne Cleanser, and I'm thoroughly impressed with its performance! The standout feature for me is the 4% Benzoyl Peroxide, which is a key acne treatment that I've been prescribed by my dermatologist. It's great to see this active ingredient in a cleanser because it not only helps clear up existing acne blemishes but also works to prevent new breakouts. I started to get horrible acne after stopping birth control, and this cleanser has been a lifesaver in helping to manage it. The cleanser itself is gentle yet effective. It doesn't dry out my skin, which can sometimes happen with acne treatments, and it leaves my skin feeling clean and refreshed without any irritation. After using it consistently, I've noticed a significant improvement in the clarity of my skin, with fewer blemishes and less redness

I really wanted this cleanser to work. It was my understanding that this cleanser was a "replacement" for the Step-3 Duo Dual Action Acne Treatment cream for the Effaclar line. I really do wish that La Roche Posay would reformulate that cream. The original 3 step system was perfect for my skin and now I'm back to breaking out at 34 yrs old, like I did when I was 15 and stressing about it isn't helping. I've never done well with cream cleansers as a combo-oily, sensitive skin user. I don't feel that they penetrate well enough through daily oil and grime, even after doing an oil/makeup removing cleanser. With that said, only using the SA Cleanser and Toner with the retinoid gel as a substitute step 3 isn't cutting it - I also add in Niacinamide, Hyaluronic Acid and Retinol serums into that regimen. However, in an effort to use up the bottle (since this is a higher cost brand), I've been using the cream cleanser in the mornings and the gel cleanser in the evenings. I haven't seen a change in the last 3-4 months since I bought it. LRP has been really good to my skin in the last 5-6 years, and I really hope they are working to reformulate the BP cream to move back to the original 3-step system for the Effaclar line. I really don't want to have to do research for another skin care brand and go through the whole process again of seeing if it works.

avis.titre: Solid Cleanser with Noticeable Results Over Time
avis.texte: I've been using the La Roche-Posay Effaclar Duo Dual Action Acne Cleanser for a while now, and overall, I really like it! I didn't experience any dryness or irritation, which can be hard to find with acne products. Over time, it did help improve my skin and reduce breakouts, though I wish it had been a bit more effective in speeding up that process. I found it works best when paired with another cleanser and rotated between morning and night use. It's not a miracle product, but it definitely made a noticeable difference with consistent use.

The texture is creamy, yet it lathers up nicely when you apply water, providing a soft foam that doesn't feel too harsh on the skin. The scent is light and non-irritating, which I appreciate given that benzoyl peroxide can sometimes have a strong, chemical smell. This cleanser is relatively gentle in comparison.

I have been using benzoyl peroxide cleansers for years since my dermatologist recommended it to treat my acne, and have seen a significant reduction in the frequency of my breakouts since using it. This was my first time trying La Roche-Posay's version, but they are a brand I have trusted for years. This cleanser works just as well as any other benzoyl peroxide cleanser I've tried, so there are cheaper options out there if you aren't willing to splurge on this one. I would recommend using this in the shower since benzoyl peroxide can bleach clothing. That is not specific to this product, but something common among all benzoyl peroxide based products. They can be great on acne-prone skin, but terrible for clothing, so I find that using it in the shower and rinsing thoroughly is the best way to avoid accidentally damaging any clothes.
